source_row.stem: A nurse learns that an elevated osmolar gap (difference between measured and calculated serum osmolality) can indicate:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The presence of unmeasured osmotically active substances, such as certain toxic alcohols","B":"Improved renal function, an interpretation not typically associated with a widened osmolar gap","C":"A finding generally considered to carry no meaningful clinical significance in a critically ill client","D":"Normal metabolic status, despite the gap reflecting the presence of unmeasured osmotically active substances"}}
source_row.rationale: An elevated osmolar gap suggests the presence of unmeasured osmotically active substances in the blood, such as toxic alcohols (methanol, ethylene glycol), prompting further toxicology evaluation.
source_row.source_name: Clinical Toxicology References — Osmolar Gap Interpretation
